pairs.registryProposal: Coverage: src-tauri/src/companion/session/* (launch.rs argv builder, cli.rs stale-resume classifier is_stale_session_error, probe_engines availability probe) belongs to NO context in this repo's context-map.json, so the companion's whole CLI transport is unreachable by any pair; this verdict had to anchor through the chat-bubbles UI context. That is a consumer context-map hole, not a registry hole - but it means the subject's strongest realization in this repo (an engine-aware launch seam with a shim-immune probe, launch.rs:24-27) is invisible to /conform.

pairs.evidence: src/hooks/execution/usePersonaExecution.ts:157 the live execution surface receives only a prose error string (ExecutionStatusEvent.error, src-tauri/core/src/types.rs:800) - the runner reads the CLI result envelope's subtype and mints a typed error_category (src-tauri/src/engine/runner/mod.rs:3624, :3646) but neither travels on the status event, so this caller cannot branch on max-turns vs usage-limit vs startup-stall and renders all of them as one '[ERROR] <text>' line.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/core/src/types.rs:800 ExecutionStatusEvent carries `error: Option<String>` only; the tool's own classification is flattened into text by parser::terminal_error_message (src-tauri/src/engine/runner/mod.rs:3624) before it reaches usePersonaExecution.ts:167 - 'the subtype must reach the caller as a value it can branch on, not be flattened into one opaque message' (verdict-survives-boundary). error_category reaches only the aggregate observability breakdown, never the live run
